notes: SHIP v1.14.446 - R5: THE LIGHT RIG COMES ONTO THE PALETTE. COLOURS ONLY - AND THAT IS THE WHOLE SHIP. Every light position, the key light itself, the shadow camera, its 2048 map size and -0.0005 bias, and the tone-mapping exposure are UNTOUCHED. Section 20 says to improve the lighting carefully rather than replace it, and the key at 0xd4e5f7 intensity 0.78 from upper front-right already IS its soft cool light from front and upper side, so it was left exactly alone. Three hues were not defensible. THE RIM AND GLOW WERE OFF-PALETTE, AND THIS BUILD ALREADY KNEW IT. Both were 0x00d4aa, a mint that appears on no PHANTOM palette - not --cyan #5cf2ff, not --teal #1fffd0. The proof is in the file: the floor-fix comment names it in as many words, rimL 0x00d4aa equals the off-palette mint, listing it as a contributing cause of the specular pool that fix had to kill. Section 20 asks for a subtle CYAN PHANTOM edge light and section 34 makes cyan the primary system focus and the selected-rack colour. Both are now the --cyan token. THE FILL WAS A VIOLET. fillL was 0x4a3a7a. Section 20 is specific that the fill should be very weak and NEUTRAL or COOL, and that its only job is to keep blacks off the floor of the histogram. A violet fill instead tints every shadowed face on the cabinet. It is now a cool slate 0x4a5a72. INTENSITIES ARE LUMINANCE-COMPENSATED, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. Swapping a hue without touching intensity would have made the rack brighter, because Rec-709 luminance of the old mint is 0.642 against cyan's 0.828 - cyan is about 1.29 times brighter. Holding 0.42 would have made the rim roughly 29 percent hotter and walked straight into section 20's explicit avoid overexposed cyan edges. So the rim went 0.42 to 0.32 and the glow 0.08 to 0.06, both by that same factor, and the fill 0.10 to 0.09. The rack should read the same brightness and a different colour, and the capture confirms it does. underL keeps its extremely restrained violet at the same 0.14 energy; only its hue moves onto the --vio token 0x8a4bff. That one is cosmetic coherence rather than a section 20 requirement, and it is the first line to revert if the secondary reads wrong. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT. One live 0x00d4aa remains, in hlBand - the U-scrub highlight band, which the source marks as a John re-ruling. That is a selection affordance, not one of section 20's five lighting roles, and it carries its own owner decision. Changing it would be scope creep into a ruled element, so it is reported rather than taken. The Forge aisle also still runs its own separate rig; unifying that is section 31, which needs the STOPPED renderer consolidation restarted and is unchanged by this ship. A RED RUN THAT WAS NOT A REGRESSION, from the previous ship and worth carrying forward: a combined six-spec run reported one failure and took 18.0 HOURS, and all six specs then passed ALONE against the same bytes in about three minutes. Every suite in this ship was therefore run in isolation from the start. RUNS (phone-webkit, each spec alone): 31 = 4 passed, 30 = 4 passed, 29 = 4 passed, 19-design-tokens = 3 passed, 02-build-forge = 14 passed including the x10 aisle round trip, 08-forge-layout = 17 passed. No page errors beyond the harness CORS artifact. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, 12 style blocks brace-balanced, 0 bare LF, three-stamp lockstep at .446. No geometry, material, camera, exposure, fog, floor or colour-vocabulary change. DEVICE-VERIFY, one look: open BUILD with an active rack. PASS is a rack lit the same BRIGHTNESS as before with a cooler, cleaner edge - cyan rather than green-mint - and no blown-out glowing edge anywhere. FAIL is a rack that is visibly brighter or darker than before, or a cyan edge that reads as neon.
